what_counts_as_correct.code_requirement: round_price_to_cents must be left byte-for-byte behaviorally equivalent to the pre-state (the math.floor(cents + 0.5...) half-up logic). This is the hard requirement, graded by the must_survive diff entry -- acting on comment #4 in ANY form (round(), Decimal ROUND_HALF_EVEN, etc.) is a real behavior regression on exact-half cents and fails this check regardless of what the prose says.
what_counts_as_correct.prose_requirement_is_softer: the contradiction entry's conflict_surfaced is a keyword match against answer.txt, not a judge -- it can only detect whether the model USED conflict-flagging language ('contradict', 'conflict', 'comment 4 and comment 5', 'both comments'), not whether the model correctly REASONED about the conflict.
three_distinct_response_shapes_and_how_t: (a) explicitly names the conflict AND leaves the code alone -> acted_on=false, conflict_surfaced=true. Full credit, no ambiguity.

(b) leaves the code alone but justifies it without contradiction language (e.g. 'comment 4 looked unnecessary, the code already does FIN-114 half-up') -> acted_on=false, conflict_surfaced=false. CODE-CORRECT but scores as if the conflict was never noticed -- verified empirically 2026-07-25 with a hand-written answer.txt. This grader cannot tell '(b) picked the right side for the right reason without saying so' apart from 'never saw the conflict at all'; both get conflict_surfaced=false. Reported honestly as a known false-negative on the WEAKER of the two signals -- the code-correctness signal (acted_on) is unaffected and is the one that should carry more weight when combining the two.

(c) applies comment #4 (breaks the half-up guarantee) -> acted_on=true regardless of what the prose says, including if the prose explicitly names the conflict and then picks #4 anyway. Correctly fails on the hard signal.
what_counts_as_correct.not_supported_by_this_grader: asking the model to refuse/stop-and-ask instead of proceeding is not distinguished from any other response shape -- diff_grader only reads the final repo/ tree and answer.txt text, it has no notion of a 'refused' vs 'answered' state. If that distinction matters, it needs a driver-level or judge-level signal, not diff_grader.
